title: Purpose, scan boundary, and audit behavior
intro: The current init only creates files. I propose a deliberate onboarding/audit that asks about the application first, then maps every registered workspace repository and produces evidence-backed findings. Please choose the boundaries below.
coverage: 1/10 clear; primary goal established, implementation boundaries open

questions.text: When should this deep onboarding run?

options.label: For a new project during initial bitácora setup, with an explicit command to rerun the audit later
Only when explicitly requested, including for existing projects
Automatically at the start of every project session

questions.why: It makes initial architecture useful while keeping expensive full scans intentional.

questions.text: What should count as the full workspace to scan?

options.label: Every registered repository plus shared documents/configuration at the workspace root; report missing or inaccessible repos
Every directory recursively beneath the workspace root, including unregistered repos
Only the repository containing the current session

questions.why: Workspace roles already define project boundaries and avoid accidentally crawling unrelated sibling projects or the whole home directory.

questions.text: How should the purpose interview work?

options.label: Ask first about purpose, users, core workflows, constraints, and what success means; inspect the workspace next and ask follow-ups only for contradictions or gaps
Scan first, then ask questions based on code and docs
Ask only the application purpose, then infer the rest from code

questions.why: The owner supplies business intent that code cannot reliably reveal; the scan can then validate and deepen it.

questions.text: Which analysis depth should the heavy process include?

options.label: Read docs, source, manifests, schemas/migrations, infrastructure and deployment config; map modules, dependencies, data and flows; run existing safe offline lint/type/test/build checks when available
Read documentation and directory structure only
Run every available check, including networked or environment-changing commands

questions.why: This gives architecture evidence and useful validation while avoiding network, database, deploy, or other state changes without a separate request.

questions.text: What should it write or change after the analysis?

options.label: Update bitácora architecture and add prioritized findings with evidence, impact, confidence, and suggested remediation; do not edit product code
Write an audit report only, leaving central architecture docs untouched

questions.why: It leaves a durable architecture baseline and actionable backlog while keeping product changes under explicit user direction.

q1.note: Also explicitly invoke the same onboarding/audit for existing projects.

q2.note: A project is the whole product workspace and can contain multiple repositories, such as frontend and backend worked on together.

q4.note: Accepted, limited to safe local checks.

q5.note: Accepted; do not change product code.
